the cab stand outside the Hippodrome
Kaplan’s drugstore with the soda fountain
the El platform at Twenty-Third Street
the victim’s walk-up over the drugstore

objects.name: a folded stack of evening papers

people.name: Cornelius Mulcahy
people.role: a young man living on expectations

secret.label: Buying morphine
secret.description: Mulcahy buys morphine at Kaplan’s from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM and would rather be thought a murderer than a hop-head.

people.name: Harrison Thorndike
people.role: a stringer for the evening papers
people.relationshipToVictim: a witness against the people the victim worked for

secret.label: Gambling debt
secret.description: Thorndike slips off to Dolan’s from 10:00 PM to settle with a bookmaker.

people.name: Carmela Vitale
people.role: a widow with rooms on the avenue
people.relationshipToVictim: the victim’s neighbour across the airshaft

secret.label: A child boarded out
secret.description: Vitale goes to Kaplan’s from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM to see a child nobody is supposed to know about.

secret.label: Murder
secret.description: Dandridge is at the office from 10:00 PM to 11:00 PM, alone with Ashby when it happens at 11:00 PM.

motive.description: was about to be exposed by the victim

people.name: Rudolf Reinhardt
people.role: a bookmaker in a small way

secret.label: Forged identity
secret.description: Reinhardt is not the person the papers say. Nothing about the evening is hidden; the lie is all in the paperwork.

motive.description: blamed the victim for a ruin

secret.label: Gambling debt
secret.description: Hauck slips off to the cab stand from 6:30 PM to 7:00 PM to settle with a bookmaker.

method.name: strangling with a cord
method.bodyEvidence: A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.

Ashby was found at the office. His watch glass broke against the floor and the hands have not moved since. The ice was brought in at 11:00 PM and the iceman’s book has the delivery timed and signed for.
The coroner puts death between 9:30 PM and 11:00 PM — two hours of nothing useful. A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.
A length of sash cord is gone from the walk-up. A cut end of the same hemp is still tied to the fitting it was taken from.

Mulcahy says Ashby told Dandridge that the story would run whether Dandridge liked it or not.

Dandridge says Reinhardt said Ashby had taken everything and would be made to feel it.

Vitale says Ashby told Hauck that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Thorndike hired us, and wants it known that Dandridge was about to be exposed by the victim, and would rather we started there.
Hauck on Mulcahy: Mulcahy’s sleeves are buttoned at the wrist in a warm room.
Tillman on Mulcahy: Somebody at Kaplan’s sells what a druggist will not, and Mulcahy knows which door.
Moretti on Mulcahy: Mulcahy was steady at nine and shaking at seven, and it was not nerves about the police.
A paper of powder at Kaplan’s, folded the way one particular hand folds them.
A prescription blank at Kaplan’s signed by a doctor who has been dead since the spring.
The man who sells it at Kaplan’s gives it up rather than be held: Mulcahy was there from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM, and stayed until it took hold.
The doctor Mulcahy used to see confirms the habit and the hour: Mulcahy was at Kaplan’s from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM, and could not have crossed the street unhelped.
Tillman on Thorndike: Thorndike was asking around for a hundred dollars in a hurry earlier in the week.
Moretti on Thorndike: A man nobody knew was waiting for Thorndike at Dolan’s and would not give a name.
Vitale on Thorndike: Thorndike goes very quiet when the racing wire is mentioned.
Betting slips at Dolan’s in Thorndike’s pocketbook, all of them losers, all of them this month.
A book of markers at Dolan’s with Thorndike’s initials against four of them.
The bookmaker’s runner is found and will say it: Thorndike was at Dolan’s from 10:00 PM paying off eleven hundred dollars, a dollar at a time, and went nowhere near the killing.
The book at Dolan’s has the payment entered against Thorndike’s name and the time beside it, from 10:00 PM, in the clerk’s own hand.
Hauck on Vitale: Vitale sends money out of every pay envelope and cannot say where it goes.
Tillman on Vitale: A woman at Kaplan’s asked for Vitale by a name Vitale has not used in years.
Moretti on Vitale: Vitale keeps a photograph and will not be asked about it twice.
A board-and-keep receipt at Kaplan’s, monthly, eight years of them.
A child’s shoe at Kaplan’s, and nobody at Kaplan’s has any children.
The woman who keeps the child says it straight out: Vitale was at Kaplan’s from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM, the same as every week, and left with the same face as always.
The parish register at Kaplan’s has the christening in it, and the board money receipted through the evening in question.
Thorndike on Reinhardt: Reinhardt’s registration card gives an address on a street that does not exist.
Dandridge on Reinhardt: Two signatures of Reinhardt’s, a month apart, are in different hands.
Petrosino on Reinhardt: Reinhardt answers to the name a half-second late, every time.
A union card in Reinhardt’s coat lining carries a different surname and a 1919 date.
A steamship ticket stub among Reinhardt’s things, in the name of a man who died at Belleau Wood.
The name Reinhardt was born with turns up on a desertion warrant from 1918. Reinhardt has been hiding from the Army for eleven years and from nobody else.
The papers are forged and the reason is plain: Reinhardt was put out of the country once already and does not mean to be put out twice.
